A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by immutable reference, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Base version:** the edit form carries `item_base`, a SHA-256 hash of the item's stored `title`, `slug`, and `body` as the page loaded them. The form saves all three, so all three are covered. A hash of the body alone would let a stale tab overwrite someone else's newer title or slug. On save, if the stored item's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the whole save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged, and no field is written.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `item_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). The remaining Markdown is rendered, and the token becomes the read-only block. The block's **raw Markdown bytes never reach the browser**: not in the Editor's HTML, not in a hidden field, not in an attribute. What the writer sees is that block's **sanitized rendered HTML** from the ordinary pipeline, displayed read-only next to its token.\n  - **On save:** each token in the posted HTML is replaced by the original fragment taken from the **stored database body** (checked by `item_base`), never from anything the client sent. A token that doesn't exist in the stored body, or appears more than once, refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block, which is allowed.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor. Consequence (approved): a relative path typed by hand, e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)`, renders as plain text, because it would break depending on page depth. Site links are made with the picker.\n- **Images follow the same rule:** only `image:<name>` renders an `<img>`. An absolute image URL (e.g. `![Logo](https://…)`) renders nothing (approved). A hot-linked image sits outside the draft gate that ADR-004 exists for. T14 updates `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py`'s \"other image URLs\" test to match.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 32 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(16)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused. A new ref is checked, in the same transaction as the insert, against **both** tables' live refs and `deleted_refs`. On the (extremely unlikely) collision, a fresh ref is generated and the insert retried, and it fails loudly after 3 attempts.\n  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.\n  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.\n  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.\n  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.\n  - **Attribute values:**\n    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.\n    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.\n    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.\n    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.\n  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.\n  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n- **Round trip:**\n  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n  - The Editor HTML for a body with locked blocks contains their tokens and their sanitized rendered HTML, and none of their raw Markdown bytes anywhere in the response.\n  - A save with an unknown locked token, a duplicated token, or a forged token that carries its own content is refused. A save with a token removed drops only that block.\n  - A save against a stale `item_base` is refused and changes nothing. **Title/slug conflict:** tab A opens an item, tab B changes only its title (or only its slug) and saves, then tab A saves an untouched body. Tab A's save is refused, and tab B's title and slug survive. A save with `body_dirty=0` stores the old body even when the posted HTML differs.\n- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview, at every page depth.\n  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n  - **Reuse:** delete the Report a link points to, create a new Report (which may take the old id), and the link is still plain text and marked \"Item deleted\", never a link to the new Report.\n  - Refs are backfilled for existing rows, unique, and unchanged by editing the title or slug.\n  - A new item's ref never equals a ref in `deleted_refs`. Tested by forcing the generator to return a tombstoned ref first: the insert retries and succeeds with a different one.\n  - An absolute image URL in a body renders no `<img>`.\n  - `http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute, and relative hand-typed hrefs submitted through the Markdown fallback render as plain text.\n  - The crawler still fails on a root-absolute or non-`https`/`mailto` absolute URL, and a test proves it by injecting one.\n- **Tables:** Excel-style HTML becomes a Markdown table. Numeric-column detection works across the formats listed above.\n- **Charts:**\n  - Grammar: every required key missing, every unknown key, every wrong type, duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity`, over-long strings, newlines in strings, mismatched `values` lengths, too many categories or series, and a block over 32 KB are each rejected, **on both the Editor and the Markdown fallback save paths**. Canonical serialization is stable (saving it again changes nothing).\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - **Structural allowlist test:** for a set of charts (every type, 1 and 4 series, negatives, missing and suppressed cells, all optional fields), the rendered figure is parsed with `html.parser`. The test collects every element name and every attribute name and asserts both sets are subsets of the fixed vocabulary. It asserts every `fill`/`stroke` is a palette constant, every `class` is a fixed name, and every `id` matches `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, with no `href`, `style`, or `on*` anywhere.\n  - Hostile writer strings (`<script>`, `\"><svg onload=…>`, `javascript:`, `</title>`, `&`) in every text field appear only as escaped text content, which the same parse confirms.\n  - Placeholders: a writer who types the placeholder shape into the body gets it rendered as inert text. Two charts get distinct placeholders.\n  - An invalid block reaching render outputs only the fixed \"could not be shown\" text.\n  - Bar charts have a zero baseline. \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation. The privacy note appears exactly once.\n- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. A draft Report appears in its own preview's nav but not in any other page or preview. Nothing is saved. Login and CSRF are required.\n- **Draft leak and export:** T08's crawl test still passes, with no draft content in `site/`, and the export is still identical to the live site.\n- **Browser behaviour** (toolbar, paste, the table controls, the chart dialog, the unsaved-changes warning) is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari. These checks add to the pytest suite and never replace it. Each ticket's closing comment records, for each check:\n  - the browser and exact version\n  - the viewport size\n  - the actions performed, step by step\n  - the observed result, with pass or fail\n  - the screenshots as supporting evidence\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Pie, stacked, scatter, and dual-axis charts. Chart colour choice.\n- Autosave, revision history, and collaborative editing.\n- Uploading a pasted or dropped picture (it's refused, with a pointer to \"Insert image\").\n- A Markdown source toggle for writers.\n- Underline, fonts, colours, text alignment, code blocks, horizontal rules.\n- Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI), which is ADR-004 unchanged.\n- Site preview of list pages (home, Data Bites index). The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- #15 T12: Site preview\n- #16 T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- #17 T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- #18 T15: Tables in the Editor\n- #19 T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- #20 T17: Chart builder\n- #21 T18: Chart images in the Editor\n\n\n=== CONTEXT\n# Kenyon Office of Institutional Research (IR) CMS\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\nADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\npublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Chart image**:\nAn *uploaded* PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a chart made in Excel, R,\nor Tableau) that a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its body and\nstored there as `image:<name>`. It belongs to its item and is published with\nit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\nReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n\n**Chart**:\nA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\npasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\navailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\nwriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n\n**Editor**:\nThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\ntables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\nThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n\n**Site preview**:\nA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\nsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\nnothing and publishes nothing.\n_Avoid_: live view\n\n**Confirmation**:\nThe one-line message the admin console shows, once, after a save, publish,\nupload, delete, or user change succeeds (`app/flash.py`). Fixed text only:\nnever a title, email, filename, or password. A refused action gets an error,\nnot a Confirmation.\n_Avoid_: flash, toast, notification, success message\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n=== {"parentUuid":"56cb800d-60ea-484e-aac7-e39413a55263","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"fad55ecc-8406-451a-8f08-d2791da5b5dd","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Xbt6LcSPoNmPgFQXw1VR8t","type":"tool_result","content":"1:title:\tSpec: Document-style authoring — Editor, tables, Charts, Site preview\n2-state:\tOPEN\n3-author:\tDavelleAT (Davelle Ampofo-Twumasi)\n4-labels:\tspec\n--\n19:The office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n20-\n21:Goal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. {"parentUuid":"f0e0cdc4-aa17-4231-b28a-4a15f215374c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"fad55ecc-8406-451a-8f08-d2791da5b5dd","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TcLsnxgNcM8y8mAooDLt25","type":"tool_result","content":"  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\nADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\npublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Chart image**:\nAn *uploaded* PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a chart made in Excel, R,\nor Tableau) that a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its body and\nstored there as `image:<name>`. It belongs to its item and is published with\nit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\nReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n\n**Chart**:\nA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\npasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\navailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\nwriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n\n**Editor**:\nThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\ntables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\nThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n\n**Site preview**:\nA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\nsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\nnothing and publishes nothing.\n_Avoid_: live view\n\n**Confirmation**:\nThe one-line message the admin console shows, once, after a save, publish,\nupload, delete, or user change succeeds (`app/flash.py`). Fixed text only:\nnever a title, email, filename, or password. A refused action gets an error,\nnot a Confirmation.\n_Avoid_: flash, toast, notification, success message\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n=== ite_edit.html\ntemplates/admin/data_bites.html\ntemplates/admin/forbidden.html\ntemplates/admin/home.html\ntemplates/admin/report_edit.html\ntemplates/admin/reports.html\ntemplates/admin/users.html\ntemplates/base.html\ntemplates/login.html\ntemplates/public/_lists.html\ntemplates/public/data_bite.html","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"a8280673-3a3f-4cde-8f05-f574ea3008a7","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:36:03.960Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n\nA CMS for Kenyon College's Office of Institutional Research: a two-person office\n(Director + Analyst/intern staff) that publishes survey results, data briefs,\nand durable reference documents like the Factbook and Common Data Set.\n\n## Language\n\n**Director**:\nThe admin role. Modeled on the real office's Associate VP for Institutional\nResearch — the only person who can publish or edit a Report, manage user\naccounts, and deactivate access.\n_Avoid_: Admin, superuser\n\n**Analyst**:\nThe editor role. Each intern gets their own named Analyst account (see\nADR-003). Can draft and publish Data Bites directly; can draft but not\npublish or edit Reports. Any Analyst may edit any other Analyst's draft\n(shift continuity), though the original author is preserved.\n_Avoid_: Editor, intern (interns are Analysts, not a separate role), staff\n\n**Data Bite**:\nA Post: a short, dated item — a survey result, an enrollment snapshot, an\nannouncement. The frequent, low-stakes content type. Analysts can publish\nthese without Director approval.\n_Avoid_: Update, post, announcement, article\n\n**Report**:\nA Page: a durable, cite-able reference document — the Factbook, a Common Data\nSet, the Survey Coordination Policy. Appears in public navigation. Only the\nDirector can publish or edit a Report, even one an Analyst drafted.\n_Avoid_: Page, document\n\n**Draft**:\nContent (a Data Bite or Report) that has been saved but not published. Never\nappears on the public site. Used for unreleased data, e.g. enrollment numbers\nstill being verified before the official count.\n_Avoid_: Unpublished, pending\n\n**Published**:\nContent visible on the public site. The one-way gate: a Report only crosses\nit with Director action.\n_Avoid_: Live, public\n\n**Chart image**:\nAn *uploaded* PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a chart made in Excel, R,\nor Tableau) that a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its body and\nstored there as `image:<name>`. It belongs to its item and is published with\nit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\nReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n\n**Chart**:\nA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\npasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\navailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\nwriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n\n**Editor**:\nThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\ntables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\nThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n\n**Site preview**:\nA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\nsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\nnothing and publishes nothing.\n_Avoid_: live view\n\n**Confirmation**:\nThe one-line message the admin console shows, once, after a save, publish,\nupload, delete, or user change succeeds (`app/flash.py`). Fixed text only:\nnever a title, email, filename, or password. A refused action gets an error,\nnot a Confirmation.\n_Avoid_: flash, toast, notification, success message\n\n**Factbook**:\nA specific Report: the office's running reference document of admissions,\nenrollment, diversity, and academic program statistics.\n\n**Common Data Set (CDS)**:\nA specific Report: a standardized annual institutional data submission,\npublished publicly.\n\n**Survey Calendar**:\nA specific Report: the schedule of past, current, and upcoming surveys the\noffice runs (e.g. faculty/staff surveys, external review surveys).\n=== None if the\n    33\t# item has no image of that name.\n    34\tImageSrc = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n    35\t\n    36\t_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n    37\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    38\t    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n    39\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    40\t    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n    41\t\n    42\t\n    43\tdef _chart_image_name(token) -> str | None:\n    44\t    \"\"\"The name in an `image:<name>` image token; The stored body stays raw; only this\n194\t     7\tfunction's output is ever marked safe.\n195\t     8\t\n196\t     9\tTwo additions to nh3's allowlist, both for Markdown tables:\n197\t    10\t  - `style` on a table cell, but only as exactly `text-align:left|right|center`,\n198\t    11\t    so a column's alignment (`|---:|`) survives and nothing else does.\n199\t    12\t  - the class TABLE_SCROLL on a <div>: each Markdown table is wrapped in one, so\n200\t    13\t    a wide table can scroll sideways without restyling the <table> itself.\n201\t    14\t\n202\t    15\tAnd one addition to Markdown, for chart images (ADR-004): an image whose URL\n203\t    16\tis `image:<name>` gets its URL from the `image_src` the caller passes, which\n204\t    17\tknows the item's images and where the page being rendered finds them. A name\n205\t    18\tit doesn't know, or no `image_src`, renders nothing. Any other image URL is\n206\t    19\tleft to the sanitizer.\n207\t    20\t\"\"\"\n208\t    21\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n209\t    22\t\n210\t    23\timport re\n211\t    24\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n212\t    25\t\n213\t    26\timport nh3\n214\t    27\tfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n215\t    28\tfrom markupsafe import Markup\n216\t    29\t\n217\t    30\tTABLE_SCROLL = \"content-table-scroll\"\n218\t    31\tIMAGE_REFERENCE = \"image:\"\n219\t    32\t# A chart image's name -> its URL from the page being rendered; None if the\n220\t    33\t# item has no image of that name.\n221\t    34\tImageSrc = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n222\t    35\t\n223\t    36\t_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n224\t    37\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n225\t    38\t    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n226\t    39\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n227\t    40\t    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n228\t    41\t\n229\t    42\t\n230\t    43\tdef _chart_image_name(token) -> str | None:\n231\t    44\t    \"\"\"The name in an `image:<name>` image token; None for any other image.\"\"\"\n232\t    45\t    src = token.attrGet(\"src\")\n233\t    46\t    return src.removeprefix(IMAGE_REFERENCE) if str(src).startswith(IMAGE_REFERENCE) else None\n234\t    47\t\n235\t    48\t\n236\t    49\tdef _render_image(self, tokens, idx, options, env):\n237\t    50\t    name = _chart_image_name(tokens[idx])\n238\t    51\t    if name is not None:\n239\t    52\t        url = env[\"image_src\"](name) if env.get(\"image_src\") else None\n240\t    53\t        if url is None:\n241\t    54\t            return \"\"\n242\t    55\t        tokens[idx].attrSet(\"src\", url)\n243\t    56\t    return self.image(tokens, idx, options, env)\n244\t    57\t\n245\t    58\t\n246\t    59\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"image\", _render_image)\n247\t    60\t\n248\t    61\t_TABLE_CELLS = (\"th\", \"td\")\n249\t    62\t_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {**nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n250\t    63\t                       **{cell: nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.get(cell, set()) | {\"style\"}\n251\t    64\t                          for cell in _TABLE_CELLS}}\n252\t    65\t_TEXT_ALIGN = re.compile(r\"\\s*text-align\\s*:\\s*(left|right|center)\\s*\", re.I)\n253\t    66\t\n254\t    67\t\n255\t    68\tdef _cell_alignment(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n256\t    69\t    \"\"\"Keep a table cell's `style` only as its text-align, and only if that is\n257\t    70\t    one of the three a Markdown table writes; drop every other declaration.\"\"\"\n258\t    71\t    if attribute != \"style\":\n259\t    72\t        return value\n260\t    73\t    if tag not in _TABLE_CELLS:\n261\t    74\t        return None\n262\t    75\t    for declaration in value.split(\";\"):\n263\t    76\t        if match := _TEXT_ALIGN.fullmatch(declaration):\n264\t    77\t            return f\"text-align:{match.group(1).lower()}\"\n265\t    78\t    return None\n266\t    79\t\n267\t    80\t\n268\t    81\tdef render_markdown(text: str, image_src: ImageSrc | None = None) -> Markup:\n269\t    82\t    \"\"\"`text` as sanitized HTML, its `image:<name>` references resolved by\n270\t    83\t    `image_src`.\"\"\"\n271\t    84\t    return Markup(nh3.clean(_MARKDOWN.render(text or \"\", {\"image_src\": image_src}),\n272\t    85\t                            attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n273\t    86\t                            attribute_filter=_cell_alignment,\n274\t    87\t                            allowed_classes={\"div\": {TABLE_SCROLL}}))\n275\t    88\t\n276\t    89\t\n277\t    90\tdef images_without_description(text: str) -> list[str]:\n278\t    91\t    \"\"\"The names in `text`'s `image:<name>` references that have no\n279\t    92\t    description (alt text), in order, for the edit page to warn of: a screen\n280\t    93\t    reader skips an image with an empty alt.\"\"\"\n281\t    94\t    return [name for block in _MARKDOWN.parse(text or \"\") for token in block.children or []\n282\t    95\t            if token.type == \"image\" and not token.content.strip()\n283\t    96\t            and (name := _chart_image_name(token)) is not None]\n284\t=== app/routes/public.py\n285\t     1\t\"\"\"The public site, served at the same paths `cms publish` exports it to. if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\n756\t    21\tAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n757\t    22\t_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n758\t    23\t# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n759\t    24\t# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n760\t    25\t_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n761\t    26\t\n762\t    27\t\n763\t    28\tclass ContentError(ValueError):\n764\t    29\t    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n765\t    30\t\n766\t    31\t\n767\t    32\tclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n768\t    33\t    pass\n769\t    34\t\n770\t    35\t\n771\t    36\tdef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n772\t    37\t    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n773\t    38\t    if not title:\n774\t    39\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n775\t    40\t    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n776\t    41\t        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n777\t    42\t                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n778\t    43\t    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n779\t    44\t        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n780\t    45\t                           \"choose another.\")\n781\t    46\t    if not body.strip():\n782\t    47\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n783\t    48\t    return title, slug, body\n784\t    49\t\n785\t    50\t\n786\t    51\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n787\t    52\tclass ContentTable:\n788\t    53\t    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n789\t    54\t    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n790\t    55\t    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n791\t    56\t    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n792\t    57\t\n793\t    58\t    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n794\t    59\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n795\t    60\t            return conn.execute(\n796\t    61\t                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n797\t    62\t                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n798\t    63\t                params,\n799\t    64\t            ).fetchall()\n800\t    65\t\n801\t    66\t    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n802\t    67\t        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n803\t    68\t        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n804\t    69\t            raise exc\n805\t    70\t        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n806\t    71\t\n807\t    72\t    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n808\t    73\t               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n809\t    74\t        \"\"\"Create a draft.\"\"\"\n810\t    75\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n811\t    76\t        try:\n812\t    77\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n813\t    78\t                item_id = conn.execute(\n814\t    79\t                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id)\"\n815\t    80\t                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n816\t    81\t                    (title, slug, body, author_id),\n817\t    82\t                ).lastrowid\n818\t    83\t                if also:\n819\t    84\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n820\t    85\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n821\t    86\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n822\t    87\t        return item_id\n823\t    88\t\n824\t    89\t    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n825\t    90\t               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n826\t    91\t        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n836\t   101\t                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n837\t   102\t                ).rowcount == 1\n838\t   103\t                if changed and also:\n839\t   104\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n840\t   105\t                return changed\n841\t   106\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n842\t   107\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n843\t   108\t\n844\t   109\t    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, drafts_only: bool = False,\n845\t   110\t              also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n846\t   111\t        \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.\n847\t   112\t        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. With drafts_only,\n848\t   113\t        a published item is left alone, as `update`. False if nothing was\n849\t   114\t        changed.\"\"\"\n850\t   115\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n851\t   116\t            changed = conn.execute(\n852\t   117\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n853\t   118\t                \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n854\t   119\t                (item_id, drafts_only),\n855\t   120\t            ).rowcount == 1\n856\t   121\t            if changed and also:\n857\t   122\t                also(conn, item_id)\n858\t   123\t            return changed\n859\t   124\t\n860\t   125\t    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n861\t   126\t        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n862\t   127\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n863\t   128\t\n864\t   129\t    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n865\t   130\t        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n866\t   131\t        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n867\t   132\t        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n868\t   133\t\n869\t   134\t    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n870\t   135\t        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n871\t   136\t        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n872\t   137\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n873\t   138\t            rows = conn.execute(\n874\t   139\t                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n875\t   140\t        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n876\t   141\t\n877\t   142\t    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n878\t   143\t        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n879\t   144\t\n880\t   145\t    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n881\t   146\t        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n887\t   152\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n888\t   153\t            return conn.execute(\n889\t   154\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n890\t   155\t                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n891\t   156\t                (status, item_id),\n892\t   157\t            ).rowcount == 1\n893\t   158\t\n894\t   159\t    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n895\t   160\t        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n896\t   161\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n897\t   162\t            return conn.execute(\n898\t   163\t                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n899\t"}]},"uuid":"22cd2072-da9f-471c-847c-ecbd11122f5a","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:36:13.999Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/davelleat/.claude/projects/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/77a9bbb5-4476-4402-bbd7-5d7dd9e381fa/tool-results/bqifr8bqv.txt","content":"=== app/public_site.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The public site: every page a visitor can see, each described by the path\n     2\tit has in the exported site (e.g. \"data-bites/fall-enrollment.html\").\n     3\t\n     4\tThe app serves these pages at those same paths (app.routes.public), and\n     5\t`cms publish` writes them there (app.publish), so the two render one set of pages\n     6\trather than two. slug, path in stored.items() if path}}\n=== app/rendering.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Markdown to safe HTML: the one pipeline every rendering of user-written\n     2\tMarkdown goes through, the admin preview now and the public export later.\n     3\t\n     4\tmarkdown-it-py renders (raw HTML in the Markdown is let through to it), then\n     5\tnh3 sanitizes, dropping <script>, event-handler attributes, javascript: URLs,\n     6\tand anything else not on its allowlist. The stored body stays raw; only this\n     7\tfunction's output is ever marked safe.\n     8\t\n     9\tTwo additions to nh3's allowlist, both for Markdown tables:\n    10\t  - `style` on a table cell, but only as exactly `text-align:left|right|center`,\n    11\t    so a column's alignment (`|---:|`) survives and nothing else does.\n    12\t  - the class TABLE_SCROLL on a <div>: each Markdown table is wrapped in one, so\n    13\t    a wide table can scroll sideways without restyling the <table> itself.\n    14\t\n    15\tAnd one addition to Markdown, for chart images (ADR-004): an image whose URL\n    16\tis `image:<name>` gets its URL from the `image_src` the caller passes, which\n    17\tknows the item's images and where the page being rendered finds them. A name\n    18\tit doesn't know, or no `image_src`, renders nothing. Any other image URL is\n    19\tleft to the sanitizer.\n    20\t\"\"\"\n    21\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    22\t\n    23\timport re\n    24\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n    25\t\n    26\timport nh3\n    27\tfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n    28\tfrom markupsafe import Markup\n    29\t\n    30\tTABLE_SCROLL = \"content-table-scroll\"\n    31\tIMAGE_REFERENCE = \"image:\"\n    32\t# A chart image's name -> its URL from the page being rendered; None if the\n    33\t# item has no image of that name.\n    34\tImageSrc = Callable[[str], \"str | None\"]\n    35\t\n    36\t_MARKDOWN = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\").enable(\"table\")\n    37\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_open\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    38\t    f'<div class=\"{TABLE_SCROLL}\">\\n' + self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env)))\n    39\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"table_close\", lambda self, tokens, idx, options, env: (\n    40\t    self.renderToken(tokens, idx, options, env) + \"</div>\\n\"))\n    41\t\n    42\t\n    43\tdef _chart_image_name(token) -> str | None:\n    44\t    \"\"\"The name in an `image:<name>` image token; None for any other image.\"\"\"\n    45\t    src = token.attrGet(\"src\")\n    46\t    return src.removeprefix(IMAGE_REFERENCE) if str(src).startswith(IMAGE_REFERENCE) else None\n    47\t\n    48\t\n    49\tdef _render_image(self, tokens, idx, options, env):\n    50\t    name = _chart_image_name(tokens[idx])\n    51\t    if name is not None:\n    52\t        url = env[\"image_src\"](name) if env.get(\"image_src\") else None\n    53\t        if url is None:\n    54\t            return \"\"\n    55\t        tokens[idx].attrSet(\"src\", url)\n    56\t    return self.image(tokens, idx, options, env)\n    57\t\n    58\t\n    59\t_MARKDOWN.add_render_rule(\"image\", _render_image)\n    60\t\n    61\t_TABLE_CELLS = (\"th\", \"td\")\n    62\t_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = {**nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n    63\t                       **{cell: nh3.ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.get(cell, set()) | {\"style\"}\n    64\t                          for cell in _TABLE_CELLS}}\n    65\t_TEXT_ALIGN = re.compile(r\"\\s*text-align\\s*:\\s*(left|right|center)\\s*\", re.I)\n    66\t\n    67\t\n    68\tdef _cell_alignment(tag: str, attribute: str, value: str) -> str | None:\n    69\t    \"\"\"Keep a table cell's `style` only as its text-align, and only if that is\n    70\t    one of the three a Markdown table writes; drop every other declaration.\"\"\"\n    71\t    if attribute != \"style\":\n    72\t        return value\n    73\t    if tag not in _TABLE_CELLS:\n    74\t        return None\n    75\t    for declaration in value.split(\";\"):\n    76\t        if match := _TEXT_ALIGN.fullmatch(declaration):\n    77\t            return f\"text-align:{match.group(1).lower()}\"\n    78\t    return None\n    79\t\n    80\t\n    81\tdef render_markdown(text: str, image_src: ImageSrc | None = None) -> Markup:\n    82\t    \"\"\"`text` as sanitized HTML, its `image:<name>` references resolved by\n    83\t    `image_src`.\"\"\"\n    84\t    return Markup(nh3.clean(_MARKDOWN.render(text or \"\", {\"image_src\": image_src}),\n    85\t                            attributes=_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES,\n    86\t                            attribute_filter=_cell_alignment,\n    87\t                            allowed_classes={\"div\": {TABLE_SCROLL}}))\n    88\t\n    89\t\n    90\tdef images_without_description(text: str) -> list[str]:\n    91\t    \"\"\"The names in `text`'s `image:<name>` references that have no\n    92\t    description (alt text), in order, for the edit page to warn of: a screen\n    93\t    reader skips an image with an empty alt.\"\"\"\n    94\t    return [name for block in _MARKDOWN.parse(text or \"\") for token in block.children or []\n    95\t            if token.type == \"image\" and not token.content.strip()\n    96\t            and (name := _chart_image_name(token)) is not None]\n=== app/routes/public.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The public site, served at the same paths `cms publish` exports it to. Who may do what is decided by each type's own\n     7\tmodule and routes, not here.\n     8\t\"\"\"\n     9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    10\t\n    11\timport re\n    12\timport sqlite3\n    13\tfrom collections.abc import Callable\n    14\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n    15\t\n    16\tfrom app import db\n    17\t\n    18\tSTATUS_LABELS = {\"draft\": \"Draft\", \"published\": \"Published\"}\n    19\t# Runs inside the transaction that wrote an item's row, given the connection and\n    20\t# the item's id; if it raises, the row's change is rolled back with it.\n    21\tAlsoWrite = Callable[[sqlite3.Connection, int], None]\n    22\t_SLUG_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\")\n    23\t# A slug names its item's page, <type folder>/<slug>.html, on the public site;\n    24\t# <type folder>/index.html is taken by the type's list page.\n    25\t_RESERVED_SLUGS = {\"index\"}\n    26\t\n    27\t\n    28\tclass ContentError(ValueError):\n    29\t    \"\"\"Content broke a rule; the message is safe to show.\"\"\"\n    30\t\n    31\t\n    32\tclass DuplicateSlug(ContentError):\n    33\t    pass\n    34\t\n    35\t\n    36\tdef validate(title: str, slug: str, body: str) -> tuple[str, str, str]:\n    37\t    title, slug = title.strip(), slug.strip()\n    38\t    if not title:\n    39\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a title.\")\n    40\t    if not _SLUG_PATTERN.fullmatch(slug):\n    41\t        raise ContentError(\"Slugs use lowercase letters, digits, and single \"\n    42\t                           \"hyphens, e.g. fall-enrollment.\")\n    43\t    if slug in _RESERVED_SLUGS:\n    44\t        raise ContentError(f\"The slug {slug} is reserved for the list page; \"\n    45\t                           \"choose another.\")\n    46\t    if not body.strip():\n    47\t        raise ContentError(\"Enter a body.\")\n    48\t    return title, slug, body\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n    52\tclass ContentTable:\n    53\t    \"\"\"One content type's table. `table` is a fixed identifier from this\n    54\t    codebase, never user input.\"\"\"\n    55\t    table: str  # e.g. \"reports\"\n    56\t    noun: str   # e.g. \"Report\", for messages\n    57\t\n    58\t    def _select(self, where: str, order: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    59\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n    60\t            return conn.execute(\n    61\t                f\"SELECT c.*, u.name AS author_name FROM {self.table} c\"\n    62\t                f\" JOIN users u ON u.id = c.author_id WHERE {where} ORDER BY {order}\",\n    63\t                params,\n    64\t            ).fetchall()\n    65\t\n    66\t    def _duplicate_slug_error(self, exc: sqlite3.IntegrityError, slug: str) -> DuplicateSlug:\n    67\t        \"\"\"Translate the slug's UNIQUE violation; re-raise any other constraint.\"\"\"\n    68\t        if f\"{self.table}.slug\" not in str(exc):\n    69\t            raise exc\n    70\t        return DuplicateSlug(f\"Another {self.noun} already uses the slug {slug}.\")\n    71\t\n    72\t    def create(self, title: str, slug: str, body: str, author_id: int, *,\n    73\t               also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> int:\n    74\t        \"\"\"Create a draft.\"\"\"\n    75\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    76\t        try:\n    77\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    78\t                item_id = conn.execute(\n    79\t                    f\"INSERT INTO {self.table} (title, slug, body, author_id)\"\n    80\t                    \" VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n    81\t                    (title, slug, body, author_id),\n    82\t                ).lastrowid\n    83\t                if also:\n    84\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n    85\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n    86\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n    87\t        return item_id\n    88\t\n    89\t    def update(self, item_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str, *,\n    90\t               drafts_only: bool = False, also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n    91\t        \"\"\"Edit title, slug, and body. False if\n    93\t        nothing was changed.\"\"\"\n    94\t        title, slug, body = validate(title, slug, body)\n    95\t        try:\n    96\t            with db.connect() as conn:\n    97\t                changed = conn.execute(\n    98\t                    f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?,\"\n    99\t                    \" updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   100\t                    \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n   101\t                    (title, slug, body, item_id, drafts_only),\n   102\t                ).rowcount == 1\n   103\t                if changed and also:\n   104\t                    also(conn, item_id)\n   105\t                return changed\n   106\t        except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n   107\t            raise self._duplicate_slug_error(exc, slug) from None\n   108\t\n   109\t    def touch(self, item_id: int, *, drafts_only: bool = False,\n   110\t              also: AlsoWrite | None = None) -> bool:\n   111\t        \"\"\"Mark the item as changed now, for a change outside its row (e.g.\n   112\t        its images), made by `also` in the same transaction. With drafts_only,\n   113\t        a published item is left alone, as `update`. False if nothing was\n   114\t        changed.\"\"\"\n   115\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   116\t            changed = conn.execute(\n   117\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   118\t                \" WHERE id = ? AND (status = 'draft' OR NOT ?)\",\n   119\t                (item_id, drafts_only),\n   120\t            ).rowcount == 1\n   121\t            if changed and also:\n   122\t                also(conn, item_id)\n   123\t            return changed\n   124\t\n   125\t    def get(self, item_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n   126\t        rows = self._select(\"c.id = ?\", \"c.id\", (item_id,))\n   127\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n   128\t\n   129\t    def list_all(self, status: str | None = None) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   130\t        \"\"\"Every item, or only those in `status`; most recently updated first.\"\"\"\n   131\t        where, params = (\"1\", ()) if status is None else (\"c.status = ?\", (status,))\n   132\t        return self._select(where, \"c.updated_at DESC, c.id DESC\", params)\n   133\t\n   134\t    def count_by_status(self) -> dict[str, int]:\n   135\t        \"\"\"How many items are in each status, zero included, e.g.\n   136\t        {\"draft\": 2, \"published\": 0}.\"\"\"\n   137\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   138\t            rows = conn.execute(\n   139\t                f\"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM {self.table} GROUP BY status\").fetchall()\n   140\t        return {**dict.fromkeys(STATUS_LABELS, 0), **dict(rows)}\n   141\t\n   142\t    def list_published(self, order: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n   143\t        return self._select(\"c.status = 'published'\", order)\n   144\t\n   145\t    def get_published(self, slug: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n   146\t        \"\"\"The published item with this slug; None for a draft or no such item.\"\"\"\n   147\t        rows = self._select(\"c.status = 'published' AND c.slug = ?\", \"c.id\", (slug,))\n   148\t        return rows[0] if rows else None\n   149\t\n   150\t    def set_status(self, item_id: int, status: str) -> bool:\n   151\t        \"\"\"Publish or unpublish. False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   152\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   153\t            return conn.execute(\n   154\t                f\"UPDATE {self.table} SET status = ?, updated_at = datetime('now')\"\n   155\t                \" WHERE id = ?\",\n   156\t                (status, item_id),\n   157\t            ).rowcount == 1\n   158\t\n   159\t    def delete(self, item_id: int) -> bool:\n   160\t        \"\"\"False if there is no such item.\"\"\"\n   161\t        with db.connect() as conn:\n   162\t            return conn.execute(\n   163\t                f\"DELETE FROM {self.table} WHERE id = ?\", (item_id,)).rowcount == 1\n","numLines":899,"startLine":1,"totalLines":899}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"4ba7d448-43bf-4f9c-9987-8ecddeb1eb66","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"77a9bbb5-4476-4402-bbd7-5d7dd9e381fa","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

return templates.TemplateResponse(\n    59\t        request, \"admin/home.html\",\n    60\t        {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": user,\n    61\t         \"content_types\": CONTENT_TYPES, \"counts\": counts,\n    62\t         \"status_labels\": STATUS_LABELS},\n    63\t    )\n    64\t\n    65\t\n    66\t@router.get(\"/content\")\n    67\tdef content_list(request: Request, user=Depends(current_user),\n    68\t                 content_type: TypeFilter = Query(\"\", alias=\"type\"),\n    69\t                 status: StatusFilter = \"\"):\n    70\t    \"\"\"Data Bites and Reports together, most recently updated first,\n    71\t    optionally narrowed to one type and/or one status.\"\"\"\n    72\t    items = [(ctype, item) for ctype in CONTENT_TYPES if content_type in (\"\", ctype.key)\n    73\t             for item in ctype.module.list_all(status or None)]\n    74\t    items.sort(key=lambda pair: pair[1][\"updated_at\"], reverse=True)\n    75\t    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n    76\t        request, \"admin/content.html\",\n    77\t        {\"title\": \"All content\", \"home_path\": \"/admin\", \"user\": Saves nothing.\"\"\"\n    88\t    return HTMLResponse(render_markdown(body))\n=== app/templating.py\n     1\t\"\"\"The Jinja environment the admin console and the public site render with.\"\"\"\n     2\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     3\t\n     4\tfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n     5\tfrom jinja2 import pass_context\n     6\t\n     7\tfrom app import settings\n     8\tfrom app.auth import csrf_token\n     9\tfrom app.flash import confirmation\n    10\tfrom app.rendering import render_markdown\n    11\tfrom app.users import ROLE_LABELS\n    12\t\n    13\t\n    14\t\n    15\t@pass_context\n    16\tdef path_for(context, name: str, **path_params) -> str:\n    17\t    \"\"\"The path of the admin route called `name` (its function's name), e.g.\n    18\t    path_for(\"edit_report_form\", report_id=3) -> \"/admin/reports/3\", so a\n    19\t    template never hard-codes a route's path. Admin pages only: the public\n    20\t    site links relatively (app.public_site).\"\"\"\n    21\t    return str(context[\"request\"].app.url_path_for(name, **path_params))\n    22\t\n    23\t\n    24\ttemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n    25\ttemplates.env.globals[\"path_for\"] = path_for\n    26\ttemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\n    27\ttemplates.env.globals[\"confirmation\"] = confirmation\n    28\ttemplates.env.filters[\"role_label\"] = ROLE_LABELS.get\n    29\ttemplates.env.filters[\"markdown\"] = render_markdown\n=== app/auth.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Sessions and CSRF.\n     2\t\n     3\tThe session is a signed cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, which signs with\n     4\titsdangerous). It holds only the user's id and a CSRF token. The user is\n     5\tre-loaded from the database on every protected request, so deactivating an\n     6\taccount ends its sessions at once.\n     7\t\"\"\"\n     8\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n     9\t\n    10\timport secrets\n    11\timport sqlite3\n    12\t\n    13\tfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n    14\t\n    15\tfrom app import users\n    16\t\n    17\t\n    18\tclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    19\t    \"\"\"Raised by current_user; main.py turns it into a redirect to /login.\"\"\"\n    20\t\n    21\t\n    22\tdef current_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    23\t    \"\"\"Dependency: the logged-in, still-active user, or LoginRequired.\"\"\"\n    24\t    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    25\t    user = users.get_active_user(user_id) if user_id is not None else None\n    26\t    if user is None:\n    27\t        request.session.clear()\n    28\t        raise LoginRequired\n    29\t    return user\n    30\t\n    31\t\n    32\tdef require_director(user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(current_user)) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    33\t    \"\"\"Dependency: current_user, but 403 unless they are a Director.\"\"\"\n    34\t    if not users.is_director(user):\n    35\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Directors only.\")\n    36\t    return user\n    37\t\n    38\t\n    39\tdef log_in(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    40\t    # A fresh session (and CSRF token) on login, so a pre-login cookie planted\n    41\t    # by someone else never becomes an authenticated one.\n    42\t    request.session.clear()\n    43\t    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user[\"id\"]\n    44\t    csrf_token(request)\n    45\t\n    46\t\n    47\tdef log_out(request: Request) -> None:\n    48\t    request.session.clear()\n    49\t\n    50\t\n    51\tdef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    52\t    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Templates call this.\"\"\"\n    53\t    token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    54\t    if token is None:\n    55\t        token = request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    56\t    return token\n    57\t\n    58\t\n    59\tasync def require_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    60\t    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing POST: the form's csrf_token must\n    61\t    match the session's.\"\"\"\n    62\t    form = await request.form()\n    63\t    submitted = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    64\t    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    65\t    if not (isinstance(submitted, str) and expected\n    66\t            and secrets.compare_digest(submitted, expected)):\n    67\t        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n=== app/reports.py\n     1\t\"\"\"Reports: durable, cite-able Markdown documents (the Factbook, the CDS).\n     2\t\n     3\tAny Analyst or Director may create a Report (always as a draft) and edit a\n     4\tdraft one, whoever started it (shift continuity, ADR-003). Editing never changes the author or created_at.\n     8\t\n     9\tA Report may carry one attached PDF (checked by app.uploads). The file is\n    11\tstored under settings.UPLOADS, outside site/, named by the Report's id; the\n    12\t`file_name` column says whether there is one.\n    13\t\n    14\tA Report may also carry chart images (app.chart_images, ADR-004), stored apart\n    15\tfrom its PDF, so that changing one never touches the other. Deleting a Report deletes\n    17\tits file and its images.\n    18\t\n    19\tPublic-facing code reads Reports only through `list_published` and\n    20\t`get_published`, so a draft cannot leak through it.\n    21\t\"\"\"\n    22\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n    23\t\n    24\timport sqlite3\n    25\tfrom pathlib import Path\n    26\t\n    27\tfrom app import chart_images, db, settings\n    28\tfrom app.content import AlsoWrite, ContentError, ContentTable\n    29\tfrom app.uploads import Pdf, write_atomically\n    30\tfrom app.users import is_director\n    31\t\n    32\t_TABLE = ContentTable(\"reports\", \"Report\")\n    33\t_IMAGES = \"reports\"  # the chart_images kind\n    34\tLOCKED = \"Only the Director can change a published Report.\"\n    35\t\n    36\tget = _TABLE.get\n    37\tlist_all = _TABLE.list_all\n    38\tcount_by_status = _TABLE.count_by_status\n    39\tset_status = _TABLE.set_status\n    40\tget_published = _TABLE.get_published\n    41\t\n    42\t\n    43\tclass ReportLocked(ContentError):\n    44\t    \"\"\"A published Report, and the user is not a Director.\"\"\"\n    45\t\n    46\t\n    47\tdef can_edit(report: sqlite3.Row, user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    48\t    \"\"\"The lockdown rule. `update`, `remove_file`, `add_image`, and\n    49\t    `remove_image` apply the same rule in their UPDATEs.\"\"\"\n    50\t    return report[\"status\"] == \"draft\" or is_director(user)\n    51\t\n    52\t\n    53\tdef file_path(report_id: int) -> Path:\n    54\t    \"\"\"Where a Report's attached file is stored.
