{"parentUuid":"68544375-cb27-486e-88af-25a547706294","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"fad55ecc-8406-451a-8f08-d2791da5b5dd","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/davelleat/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Review uncommitted working-tree changes against HEAD (c5d3b13) for ticket T12 (GitHub issue #15, spec #14). Exclude notes/usage-ledger.csv and docs/transcripts/."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"9956ac8a-ffca-4a2b-b89c-563dec1e94dc","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:52:50.883Z","sourceToolUseID":"toolu_01QL3fze9tfKD7FKqeMt6xk3","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"77a9bbb5-4476-4402-bbd7-5d7dd9e381fa","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main","slug":"twinkling-moseying-papert"}

Nothing is saved.\n\nThe preview's links stay relative, exactly as the export writes them; a\n<base> places the page under /admin/<type>/<id>/preview/, the preview's\nown copy of the site, which serves the stylesheet and the item's own\nchart images and file (draft or not), and sends any other page to the\npublished one. The absolute `<base href=\"/admin/...\">` and the `\"/\" + path` redirect only reach admin responses. The `public_site` module docstring now records the Site preview exception.\n  - **ADR-003:** `preview_report` uses `_editable_or_403`. `report_preview_site` uses only `_get_or_404`, which matches the existing rule that any signed-in user may download a Report's files.\n  - **CONTEXT.md vocabulary:** \"Site preview\" and \"Draft preview, not published\" are the glossary's terms, and none of the Avoid words appear.\n  \n  **Judgement calls against documented standards**\n  1. **Global CSS rule on broad selectors**, `app/public_site.py` CSS: `body:has(.admin-site-preview) { max-width: 90rem; }` targets `body`. `:has()` narrows it, but a class on the admin layout would be better. The `.admin-*` rules also ship in the public `style.css`. That follows the existing `.admin-confirmation` precedent, so it is not new.\n  2. **Match neighbouring comment density:** `new_bite_preview_site` and `new_report_preview_site` have no docstring, while every sibling route has one.\n  3. **Match neighbouring idiom:** `_stored_images(module, item)` leaves `module` untyped. `admin.py` already uses `ModuleType` for the same pattern.\n  \n  **Baseline smells (all judgement calls)**\n  - **Duplicated Code:** `_site_preview` in `routes/data_bites.py` and `routes/reports.py` is nearly identical, and so are the `preview_new_*` / `new_*_preview_site` route pairs and `form = form or {\"title\": \"\", \"slug\": \"\", \"body\": \"\"}`. Parallel modules are an existing repo pattern (the old `_image_src` was duplicated the same way), so extract a helper only if a third content type appears.\n  - **Duplicated Code:** `preview_site_file` repeats the PDF response `FileResponse(stored, media_type=\"application/pdf\", headers={\"X-Content-Type-Options\": \"nosniff\"})` from `report_file` in `routes/public.py`. Pull it into one `_pdf_response` helper.\n  - **Primitive Obsession:** `if stored.suffix == \".pdf\":  # a Report's file` chooses the response type from the file extension. Passing the kind alongside `files`, or keeping the PDF entries separate, would make it explicit.\n  - **Mysterious Name / Speculative Generality:** `def _render(self, **preview)` takes a kwargs bag that only ever holds `preview_base`. Use `preview_base: str | None = None` instead.\n  - **Shotgun Surgery:** the sort key `key=lambda found: (found[\"title\"], found[\"id\"] is None, found[\"id\"] or 0)` in `report_preview` copies the `ORDER BY c.title, c.id` in `reports.list_published`. If that order changes, the preview nav silently disagrees with the real one. Add a comment pointing to it, or expose the ordering from `reports`.\n  - **Divergent Change / Feature Envy:** `preview_site_file` serves admin-only draft files but lives in `app/routes/public.py`, whose docstring says \"everything here is published content only\". The admin route modules also now import from the public route module. That follows an existing precedent (`.admin-confirmation`), but it does ship admin-only rules in `site/style.css`.\n  - Typing in the title also refreshes the preview. That is a reasonable reading of \"unsaved edits\".\n  \n  **(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n  \n  1. The draft Report's own nav link is dead inside its preview. The spec says: \"a draft Report is in the nav of its own Site preview\". It is in the nav. The test skips exactly this link (`continue  # the draft's own page ... not public`).\n     - A related problem: every other link in the frame leaves the preview for the live public page, which has no banner.\n     - Worth one line in the closing comment, or a fix that serves the preview page itself for its own path.\n  2. \"Report file link\" and \"Nothing is saved\" both hold. One side effect: \"Preview on site\" on the Report form posts the whole multipart form, so a chosen PDF is uploaded to the preview route and thrown away unread. Nothing is saved, but it's wasteful.\n  3. \"relative links at every depth\": only item pages are previewed, and all of them sit at depth 1. So the test covers the one depth the spec allows (list pages are Out of Scope). That's fine, but \"every depth\" is effectively depth 1.\n  \n  **Verified OK**\n  - The banner appears on every preview, including published items.\n  - The preview uses the public stylesheet and templates.\n  - The nav shows the item as if published, sorted by title, with other drafts hidden.\n  - The frame sits beside the body field and drops below it under 64rem. It has the Desktop/Phone toggle, 250 ms debounce, and the \"not updating\" message.\n  - The create page has a preview with no chart images.\n  - Login and CSRF are required on the POSTs.\n  - Report edit previews use `_editable_or_403` (ADR-003). The Safari check was never done, and nothing has been posted to the issue yet. Only the Chrome screenshots exist, in `docs/screenshots/site-preview-*.jpg`, and #15 has 0 comments. This blocks closing the ticket.\n  \n  2. An unsaved slug is ignored. The spec says: \"both show the current **unsaved** edits\". The routes and the JS read only `title` and `body`, so a slug change doesn't show in the preview's hrefs or its file path. The reason is written down in `_as_if_published` and the effect is invisible to a reader, so I accept it. It should be stated in the closing comment as a deliberate deviation.\n  \n  **(b) Scope creep**\n  \n  None of substance.\n  - The read-only published-Report view for Analysts now shows a saved Site preview instead of the old admin preview. That fits \"The current admin-styled preview is replaced\".\n  - The new admin layout CSS went into `public_site.CSS`. That follows an existing precedent (`.admin-confirmation`), but it does ship admin-only rules in `site/style.css`.\n  - Typing in the title also refreshes the preview. That is a reasonable reading of \"unsaved edits\".\n  \n  **(c) Implemented, but looks wrong**\n  \n  1. The draft Report's own nav link is dead inside its preview. The spec says: \"a draft Report is in the nav of its own Site preview\". It is in the nav. But `../reports/<slug>.html` goes through `preview_site_file` and gets a 303 to the public `/reports/<slug>.html`, which returns 404 for a draft. The test skips exactly this link (`continue  # the draft's own page ... not public`).\n     - A related problem: every other link in the frame leaves the preview for the live public page, which has no banner.\n     - Worth one line in the closing comment, or a fix that serves the preview page itself for its own path.\n  2. \"Report file link\" and \"Nothing is saved\" both hold. One side effect: \"Preview on site\" on the Report form posts the whole multipart form, so a chosen PDF is uploaded to the preview route and thrown away unread. Nothing is saved, but it's wasteful.\n  3. \"relative links at every depth\": only item pages are previewed, and all of them sit at depth 1. So the test covers the one depth the spec allows (list pages are Out of Scope). That's fine, but \"every depth\" is effectively depth 1.\n  \n  **Verified OK**\n  - The banner appears on every preview, including published items.\n  - The preview uses the public stylesheet and templates.\n  - The nav shows the item as if published, sorted by title, with other drafts hidden.\n  - The frame sits beside the body field and drops below it under 64rem. The admin visual pass (out of scope, spec #14) can move admin CSS out |\n\n### Spec\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| A draft Report's own nav link in its preview went to the public page, which 404s | **Fixed.** It opens that Report's Site preview as saved (tested) |\n| Other links in the preview (home, other Reports, list pages) go to the published pages, without the banner | **By design.** List pages are out of scope (\"The preview shows only the item's own page\"), and links never reach a draft |\n| An unsaved **slug** isn't reflected | **Deliberate.** The slug changes only hrefs, which no reader sees. The preview keeps the saved slug so it finds the item's files at the paths it gives them (`public_site._as_if_published`). Title and body are live |\n| \"Preview on site\" on a Report posts the whole multipart form, a chosen PDF included, which is discarded unread | **Accepted.** Nothing is saved (tested); avoiding it needs JS on a no-JS path |\n| \"Relative links at every depth\": previewed pages all sit at depth 1 | Tested at that depth. Links go up to the root (`../style.css`) and down to depth 3 (`../images/<type>/<slug>/<name>`), and each one is fetched |\n| Safari browser check not done | **Open.** See below |\n\n### Browser check\n\n**Chrome 154.0.0.0** (macOS), local server with seeded demo content, signed in as the demo Analyst.\n\n| Viewport | Action | Observed |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1280 | Open the draft Report \"Common Data Set 2026-27\" | The frame sits beside the fields, with the banner and the public stylesheet (banner rule computed: 4px border). The nav lists the draft CDS and Survey Calendar, and the other draft is hidden. `docs/screenshots/site-preview-report-draft-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Type `## Unsaved heading` and a table in the body | The frame re-renders with an `<h2>` and a table, with no status message. `<base>` = `/admin/reports/2/preview/reports/common-data-set-2026-27.html`. `site-preview-typing-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Click \"Preview on site\" | A new tab opens at `/admin/reports/2/preview` with the same unsaved rendering and the banner. `site-preview-new-tab-1280.jpg` |\n| 1280 | Click Phone | The frame is 390px wide, and `aria-pressed` moves from Desktop to Phone |\n| 1280 | Log out in the background, then type | \"Preview is not updating. Reload the page (you may need to log in again).\" |\n| — | Check the database | The report rows are unchanged (body, `updated_at`) |\n| 390 | Open the Data Bites create page | The frame is below the fields, with the banner and an empty body. The page scrolls sideways because of the list **table** above, which predates T12 and isn't touched here. `site-preview-create-390.jpg` |\n| 390 | Edit the draft Data Bite | The frame is below \"Save changes\", with no sideways scroll (scrollWidth = innerWidth = 386). `site-preview-edit-390.jpg` |\n\nScreenshots are in the repo under `docs/screenshots/`.\n\n**Safari:** not yet checked. {"parentUuid":"2e24695d-8ab9-4bce-bde7-5924c1760312","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaDSMxAzcM2k2CBnrFdb","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've built T12 (the Site preview, #15). It's committed and passes tests and a Chrome check, but it isn't closed yet: the Safari check still needs doing, and I can't drive Safari from here. The full suite passes (337 tests, 31 of them new in `tests/test_t12_site_preview.py`).\n\n**What it does**\n- **Where it shows:** every Data Bite and Report edit page, and both create pages. It replaces the old admin-styled preview.\n- **What it shows:** the item as its public page would look if published, with the unsaved title and body. It uses the public templates, `style.css` and the site nav, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n- **Layout:** the frame sits beside the fields and drops below them on a narrow screen. It has a Desktop/Phone width toggle and updates as you type. The \"not updating\" message still appears when the session ends.\n- **Preview on site:** posts the unsaved form to a new tab. Nothing is saved, and nothing is written to `site/`.\n- **Nav:** a draft Report appears in its own preview's nav; every other draft stays hidden. The public site and the export are unchanged.\n- **How links work:** the preview's links are the same relative ones the export writes. A `<base>` tag points them at the preview's own copy of the site under `/admin/<type>/<id>/preview/`. That copy serves the stylesheet and the item's own chart images and PDF, even for a draft. Links to other pages go to the published pages, which have no banner.\n- **Permissions:** the preview routes need login and CSRF. Only the Director can preview edits to a published Report.\n- **Removed:** the old `/admin/preview` route. I moved the older T04, T06, T10 and T11 preview tests over to the Site preview.\n\n**Behaviour you might not expect**\n- **Slug:** changing the slug doesn't show in the preview until you save. It only changes link addresses, which nobody sees, and keeping the saved slug lets the preview find the item's files.\n- **PDF on \"Preview on site\":** for a Report, a PDF chosen in the form gets posted with it and thrown away unread.\n\n**Review:** I ran `/code-review`. The standards review found no hard violations; the spec review's main gap was Safari. I fixed seven of the findings in `9fd3e9e`, including moving the draft-file serving into its own module, `app/routes/site_preview.py`. I posted every finding and how it was resolved, plus the Chrome check (Chrome 154 at 1280 and 390), as a [comment on #15](https://github.com/DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/15#issuecomment-5918630687). The screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/site-preview-*.jpg`.\n\n**Commits:** `52015b8` T12: Site preview, then `9fd3e9e` review fixes. Both say \"Refs #15\", not \"Closes #15\", because of the Safari gap. I haven't pushed.\n\n**Found along the way:** at 390px the Data Bites list page scrolls sideways because of its table. That was already the case before this ticket, and I didn't change it.\n\n**What you need to do:** run the Safari check at 390 and 1280 with `uv run cms serve` and your normal demo login. On a draft Report, check:\n1. the frame sits beside the fields at 1280 and below them at 390;\n2. typing updates the frame;\n3. \"Preview on site\" opens a new tab with the same rendering;\n4. the Phone toggle narrows the frame.\n\nSend me the Safari version and what you see, and I'll add it to the #15 comment and make the closing commit ending `Closes #15`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":612,"cache_read_input_tokens":244526,"output_tokens":1198,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":612,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1198,"cache_read_input_tokens":244526,"cache_creation_input_tokens":612,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":612},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"2cf403af-c1ab-4fb1-9ebc-e76b358d4076","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfaDSMV9ACw5AQdAGBdfW","type":"assistant","uuid":"b479fa2a-a090-4884-aa81-9deb9c01ba17","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:58:19.046Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"77a9bbb5-4476-4402-bbd7-5d7dd9e381fa","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main","slug":"twinkling-moseying-papert"}
